title: Count Submatrices With Equal Frequency of X and Y
summary: Given a 2D character matrix grid with elements 'X', 'Y', or '.', count the submatrices that include grid[0][0], have an equal number of 'X' and 'Y', and contain at least one 'X'.
statement: Given a 2D character matrix grid with elements 'X', 'Y', or '.', count the submatrices that include grid[0][0], have an equal number of 'X' and 'Y', and contain at least one 'X'.
constraints: grid is a nonempty rectangle containing X, Y, or dot characters.
Count rectangles with top-left corner fixed at grid[0][0] and arbitrary bottom-right corner.
A counted rectangle contains at least one X and has equal X and Y counts.
hints: Every eligible rectangle is a two-dimensional prefix ending at one bottom-right cell.
Accumulate per-column X/Y totals by row, then running totals across columns.
For each cell add column counts to row prefix; count when X>0 and X==Y.
The accumulated totals equal exactly the origin-to-current rectangle, so testing every bottom-right corner counts each eligible rectangle once.
editorial: The accumulated totals equal exactly the origin-to-current rectangle, so testing every bottom-right corner counts each eligible rectangle once.

tests.explanation: The balanced origin-anchored rectangles ending at columns one or two of the first row and column zero of the second row total three.
Only the full 2x2 origin-anchored rectangle has one X and one Y.
